problem:
Consider the following system of linear equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}x-y+3z=2 \\ x-2y-5z=-1 \\ 2x-3y+2z=1\end{aligned}
$$

The system above has the matrix representation $Ax=b.$ Given that $x=⟨x,y,z⟩$ is unique, what is the value of $x+y+z?$ 

*Hint: The inverse of the coefficient matrix is given by*

$$
\,{A}^{-1}=-\frac{1}{4}[\begin{aligned}-19 & -7 & 11 \\ -12 & -4 & 8 \\ 1 & 1 & -1\end{aligned}].
$$

activity_context.topic_title: Solving Systems of Equations Using Inverse Matrices

feedback.problem:
Consider the following system of linear equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}x-y+z=1 \\ 3x+2y-z=1 \\ x-4y+3z=3\end{aligned}
$$

The system above has the matrix representation $Ax=b.$ Given that $x=⟨x,y,z⟩$ is unique, what is the value of $x+y+z?$ 

*Hint: The inverse of the coefficient matrix is given by*

$$
\,{A}^{-1}=-\frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}2 & -1 & -1 \\ -10 & 2 & 4 \\ -14 & 3 & 5\end{aligned}].
$$
feedback.worked_solution:
First, let's write our system in matrix form as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}Ax & =b \\ [\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 1 \\ 3 & 2 & -1 \\ 1 & -4 & 3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ 3\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Recall that the solution to $Ax=b$ is given by $x={A}^{-1}b.$

Therefore, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}x & ={A}^{-1}b \\  & =-\frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}2 & -1 & -1 \\ -10 & 2 & 4 \\ -14 & 3 & 5\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ 3\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -2 \\ -2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

So, the solution is $x=1,y=-2,z=-2.$

Finally, $x+y+z=1+(-2)+(-2)=-3.$
